answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every new identity to post a staked bond before its signal counts in consensus, with slashing if peers detect forged behavior. Each fake agent must lock real capital, and the attacker cannot let fake identities wander freely because coordinated duplicates trigger proportional forfeits, burning the stake and cutting future yield. The cost of forging an identity is therefore the bond plus the expected penalty, which scales with the number of copies, so a wide canyon opens between honest agents, who merely post a refundable deposit, and sybils,
